title: Geometric and organic forms and modelling
intro: Organic geometry needs defined references as much as rectilinear furniture. Coordinate profiles and sections, distinguish surface appearance from construction, and inspect part interfaces before releasing fabrication data.

sections.title: Define profiles and section references
sections.text: Establish floor datum, axes and view direction. Locate named sections on the plan where depth or form changes. A curved elevation does not reveal whether the body is a constant extrusion or a changing surface. Coordinate overall references across views rather than drawing each view independently.
sections.caption: Named section locations explain changing depth.

sections.title: Distinguish skin from structure
sections.text: Compare a solid form, ribs with a skin, and an assembly of shaped sections. Show support paths, interfaces and finish build-up for each. These are design strategies requiring material and fabrication review, not bending or machine-setting instructions. Identical outer silhouettes can conceal different weights, edges and service access.
sections.caption: Matching silhouettes do not imply matching construction.

sections.title: Check parts and assembly orientation
sections.text: Number parts and define face, orientation, mating surface and insertion sequence. In the example A and B are mirrored ribs, not identical same-handed copies. Exporting both as A can change the interface. Check virtual assembly and interference, then state which uncertainties need a physical sample before specialist fabrication release.
sections.caption: Mirrored parts retain distinct identities.

example.title: Worked case and decision
example.text: The outer form is correct, but B was exported with A’s handedness. Virtual assembly exposes a collision. Correct identity and orientation, then recheck the interface rather than enlarging the whole object to conceal the part error.
example.decision: Decision: correct the mirrored part and recheck assembly.

quiz.question: Does a curved elevation define the complete depth geometry?
quiz.explanation: A silhouette can conceal changing depth.

assignment.prompt: Submit coordinated profiles, construction alternatives and an A/B assembly check.

faq.question: Does virtual assembly replace every physical check?
faq.answer: No. Material and connection performance still need suitable verification.
